classification.difficultyReason: Combine opposite-direction travel, an exact time conversion and a fractional relationship between two speeds.

content.prompt: Two aeroplanes pass each other in flight while travelling in opposite directions. Each of the planes continues on its flight for 45 minutes, after which the planes are 840 km apart. The speed of the first aeroplane is $\frac{3}{4}$ the speed of the other aeroplane. Calculate the average speed of each aeroplane.

answer.short:
First aeroplane: $480\text{ km/h}$. Other aeroplane: $640\text{ km/h}$.

Their distances add to 840 km because they travel in opposite directions.
answer.worked:
The time is $45\div60=\frac34$ hour. Since the planes travel in opposite directions, their distances from the passing point add to 840 km.

Let $v$ km/h be the average speed of the other aeroplane. The first aeroplane's average speed is $\frac34v$ km/h.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac34\left(\frac34v+v\right)&=840\\\frac{21}{16}v&=840\\v&=840\times\frac{16}{21}\\v&=640\end{aligned}$$
The first aeroplane's average speed is
$$\begin{aligned}v_{\text{first}}&=\frac34\times640\\v_{\text{first}}&=480\text{ km/h}.\end{aligned}$$
The other aeroplane's average speed is $640\text{ km/h}$.
